narrative.overview: Baulr is a high-precision personal storage instrument. Designed for non-technical users who care deeply about their family media, archives, and documents, it speaks the aesthetic language of a secure, solid physical vault rather than an ephemeral SaaS web app. Every element projects calm, permanence, and non-destructive safety.
keyCharacteristics: Zero-Shadow Tonal Depth: Strictly flat surfaces layered through charcoal tonality and ghost hairline borders.
Telemetry-Led Precision: Progress bars and capacity gauges act as visual anchors, making storage status unmistakable at a glance.
Physical Reassurance: Soft pill badges, tactile feedback, and explicit non-destructive safety confirmations.

rules.name: The Zero-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay strictly flat at rest. Depth is established purely through tonal background contrast and 1px ghost borders (oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)). Drop shadows are banned.

rules.name: The Semantic Signal Rule
rules.body: Bright saturated colors (green, cyan, amber, coral) are reserved exclusively for status metrics and telemetry; decorative illustration gradients must not mimic system status indicators.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: All file sizes, transfer speeds, percentages, and time durations must render using tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) to prevent layout jitter during live sync updates.

rules.name: The Ghost Border Fallback
rules.body: Every card and surface separation must carry a 1px border. Never rely on subtle background contrast alone, ensuring crisp separation on uncalibrated or high-brightness monitors.

dos: Do format all file sizes and transfer speeds consistently using binary units (KB, MB, GB, TB) via formatBytes.
Do keep cards and surfaces strictly flat with 1px ghost borders (oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)).
Do display reassuring safety language ('Zero-loss cryptographic verify enabled', 'Moved to Trash') whenever user files are affected.
Do keep React component files under 150 lines by extracting modular sub-components.
donts: Don't use heavy, multi-layered drop shadows or glow effects on resting surfaces.
Don't use technical jargon (e.g., 'MD5 mismatch', 'RPC timeout', 'CLI exit 1') in user-facing toasts or cards.
Don't apply data-tauri-drag-region to clickable buttons, inputs, or interactive controls.
Don't use saturated accent colors decoratively on generic body text or non-interactive borders.
